instruction: Take Vim off your favorites dock.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires removing vim.desktop (the middle app) from the favorites dock. Initial setup creates favorites list ['thunderbird.desktop', 'vim.desktop', 'google-chrome.desktop']. After removing Vim, the expected result is ['thunderbird.desktop', 'google-chrome.desktop']. Uses existing check_gnome_favorite_apps metric which compares sets (order-independent). This is actually what the original task was supposed to check.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter extracts the correct state: Uses gsettings command to retrieve GNOME favorite-apps list, which is the exact state needed to verify the instruction
Metric logic is correct: check_gnome_favorite_apps parses the gsettings output and compares using set equality (order-independent), which is appropriate for verifying app removal from dock
Complete coverage: Evaluator verifies that vim.desktop is removed AND that the remaining apps (thunderbird.desktop, google-chrome.desktop) are still present
Expected values are semantically correct: ['thunderbird.desktop', 'google-chrome.desktop'] matches the initial setup minus vim.desktop, which is exactly what the instruction requires
Correct parameter handling: Metric function correctly accesses rule['expected'] when expected.type='rule', following the correct pattern for framework's get_rule()
No state timing issues: Favorite apps setting persists after task completion, no postconfig needed to access state
Will work correctly at runtime: gsettings command will successfully retrieve favorites list, eval() will parse the string output, and set comparison will correctly verify task completion
